table.n: Atlas estimate: spodumene concentrate has no customs code of its own; it is read from HS 253090 ('mineral substances not elsewhere specified'), keeping only the rows from Australia, Zimbabwe and Brazil to China, the exporters for which a page read by the atlas says they ship lithium concentrate to China (the pages are in the notes of the page): 30% of the tonnage and 67% of the value of the code in 2024. These rows may still hold other minerals. Customs gross weight of concentrate, not lithium content. CEPII BACI HS92 HS 253090 rows to China only, 2024, all transport modes, gross weight; world = sum of all reported flows in the Atlas BACI extract (flows below 1,000 t and 1 M USD omitted)

notes: 2 flows of the lithium chemicals codes (15.1 kt in 2024) are declared under 1,500 USD per tonne, the price of ore or concentrate rather than of a lithium chemical. The atlas leaves them out of the trade tables, the lanes, the chokepoint estimates and the country figures; the cause (a product or a weight misdeclared, for instance) is not established here: Nigeria to China 8.60 kt at 286 USD/t; Brazil to China 6.48 kt at 1,110 USD/t.
Trade tables and flows are lithium carbonate and hydroxide/oxide (HS 283691, 282520) in gross weight (kt), not lithium content. USGS production is contained lithium (t Li), so units differ.

Spodumene concentrate, the ore concentrate of hard-rock lithium mines, is shown in its own table (Atlas estimate from HS 253090, 5.04 Mt to China in 2024 at 738 USD per tonne on average); it is not added to the chemicals tables, whose tonnes are of another product. Australia declares its spodumene concentrate under this code: its statistics office created the national subheading 25309011 'Lithium concentrates' for it in January 2021 (Australian Bureau of Statistics, Insights into Australian Exports of Lithium, 4 August 2022, CC BY 4.0, https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/insights-australian-exports-lithium). The spodumene lanes and their route show its history from 2021 only: no page read says what the code held from these exporters before.

Pages read for the exporters of the spodumene table: Australia: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Insights into Australian Exports of Lithium, 4 August 2022, CC BY 4.0, https://www.abs.gov.au/articles/insights-australian-exports-lithium; Zimbabwe: "Most of the concentrate is exported to China for further processing" (Reuters, 3 February 2026, republished by Kitco, https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2026-02-03/zimbabwe-spodumene-exports-11-2025-revenue-flat-soft-prices); Brazil: Sigma Lithium's lithium concentrate shipped to the port of Vitoria, Espirito Santo, bound for China (the page calls it green lithium concentrate) and a cargo of lithium concentrate scheduled for Zhangjiagang, China (Diario do Comercio, 6 February 2024, and SMM (Shanghai Metals Market), 18 July 2024, https://diariodocomercio.com.br/economia/sigma-exporta-maior-carregamento-litio-minas/ and https://news.metal.com/en/newscontent/102856969).

Not read as spodumene: HS 253090 rows to China from Nigeria 0.49 Mt, Mali (no 2024 row) and Canada 0.06 Mt in 2024. They may hold lithium concentrate, but the atlas found no page that says so for these exporters, so they stay out of the spodumene table.

Lithium carbonate, oxide and hydroxide (HS 283691, 282520): the tables hold 0.489 Mt, 95% of the 0.512 Mt that the customs file records for these codes in 2024 (gross weight). The difference: 0.00812 Mt are pairs under the threshold of the extract (1,000 t and USD 1 million; 110 of the 963 pairs of the file are kept); 0.0151 Mt are taken out by the cleaning rules (tonnage re-estimated from value, or flows left out).
